todos: Verify the integrated image-generation catalog entries on the target machine: SDXL Base qualita for portraits/people, SDXL Turbo rapido for fast drafts, LCM SDXL bozza for prompt iteration, and FFusionXL creativo for illustration-oriented prompts.

Measure the new quality-to-speed image preset mapping per model: Qualita, Bilanciato, and Velocita must produce acceptable latency, memory use, prompt adherence, and fewer human anatomy failures on DirectML.

Tune model-specific generation defaults after real outputs are reviewed: keep Turbo/LCM at low guidance and low steps, keep base SDXL models at higher guidance, and adjust step counts only when visual quality improves.

Centralize remaining image UI help text into compact tooltips: model choice, preset slider, format, seed, negative prompt, download consent, and catalog editor should avoid long visible explanatory paragraphs.

Make runtime packaging deterministic for Windows: ensure desktop debug, publish, and installer outputs are runtime-specific win-x64 by default and include the native ONNX Runtime files needed by the DirectML package.

Normalize the existing .NET formatting baseline so dotnet format OnlyRag.sln --verify-no-changes can pass without unrelated churn: fix repository-wide CRLF/LF inconsistencies, final newline issues, and whitespace formatting in the preexisting App, Core, Infrastructure, and Api test files; do this as a dedicated formatting-only change and rerun dotnet format verification afterward.

Manually verify integrated image generation on the target NVIDIA machine after cleanup: model download, snapshot verification, runtime status showing DirectML before generation, prompt generation, saved gallery entry, generated file retrieval, and no fallbackReason unless DirectML actually fails.

Manually verify CPU image fallback after cleanup by disabling GPU preference or forcing a DirectML initialization failure, then confirm runtime status shows CPU with a clear fallbackReason and generation still saves retrievable images.

Run representative runtime workflows on the target deployment scope after legacy removal: real OCR on scanned PDF/image with NVIDIA runtime and CPU fallback, real Qdrant document import/search/chat indexing, Ollama chat/embedding/translation using chosen local models, and LibreOffice PDF translation export.

Monitor and add the next OCR NVIDIA CUDA runtime target beyond cuda130 only when PaddlePaddle publishes stable Windows win_amd64 paddlepaddle-gpu wheels for newer CUDA SDK targets such as cu132 or cu133; update runtime-manifest.json, requirements-nvidia-cu*.txt, Test-OcrRuntimeCatalog.ps1, then verify the installed app provisions and uses the new GPU runtime successfully.
